headings: # Sometimes There Isn't a Clear Child Yet
intro: The new h2's heading and its first paragraph.

rows.label: New: what to untangle from, and where it turns into a bargain
rows.article: Part of building who you are is untangling yourself
source: Identity formation also requires untangling from family emotional systems
Most social systems ask for some conformity.
notes: The guide's first two paragraphs of this h2, as one. The article already has the controlling family, the strict church and the relationship you keep up a fake version of yourself for, so this paragraph adds the rest: groups and political tribes, kind families and religions, ordinary conformity, and what families and friends ask.

Writer 2 of the second round, with four fixes from the reviews: a last sentence on where ordinary conformity turns into the bargain (a fresh reader couldn't tell); "the expectations of" a kind family or religion, so what you untangle from is the pull, not the family or faith (a grounding); "or get upset about" for the guide's rules about emotion; and "Going along with those…" as its own sentence, so the paragraph doesn't march.

Left out: what religions and political tribes ask (particular beliefs and behavior; consistent positions and predictable reactions). The one draft that carried the tribe's read AI, and the guide comes back to both later in this h2. Say if you want either here.
Pangram: alone 100% Human (99); the h2 100% Human (103); the h1 100% Human (793).

carries.draft: Part of building who you are is untangling yourself from whatever pulls you away from your own knowing in return for belonging, like a political tribe or another group you identify with.
carries.guide: Identity formation also requires untangling from family emotional systems, religious orthodoxies, group identities, political tribes, and individual relationships that pull you away from your own knowing in exchange for belonging.

carries.draft: Or the expectations of a family or religion that's kind to you.
carries.note: "kind to you": not only the harsh ones the article already has

carries.draft: Going along with those might just feel like being good.
carries.note: a grounding singled it out: a kind family's pull comes as warmth, not fear

carries.draft: Most groups expect some conformity, which is ordinary, like your family wanting a particular kind of son or daughter,
carries.guide: Most social systems ask for some conformity. Families want a particular kind of son, daughter, or sibling.

carries.draft: or your friends' rules about what you can joke about or get upset about.
carries.guide: Friend groups develop rules about acceptable topics, humor, and emotion.

carries.draft: But if going along means betraying yourself, that's the bargain.
carries.guide: Self-differentiation means noticing where belonging is being purchased with self-betrayal
